items.title: Countable indexedness ascends and descends along a representable surjective flat morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces which is representable, surjective and flat, the lemma asserts that the source is countably indexed if and only if the target is (statement lines 4548-4553). One direction is a citation; the other is a real argument. Assuming the source countably indexed, one writes both spaces as filtered colimits, and for each stage of the source finds a stage of the target through which it factors; conversely, for each stage of the target, the fibre product with the source is an affine scheme and therefore factors through some stage of the source (proof lines 4555-4568). The author then displays the resulting diagram and observes that the proof is complete once the dotted arrow -- a factorisation of one stage of the target through a later one -- exists (proof lines 4568-4574). That existence is established by choosing a stage above the two in question, translating the two closed subschemes into ideals of its coordinate ring, and using the hypothesis: the relevant fibre product is faithfully flat over the stage of the target, so the containment of the two ideals after extending along the source morphism descends to a containment of the ideals themselves (proof lines 4574-4589). Since the stages selected form a cofinal countable subsystem, the target is countably indexed (proof lines 4571-4576). The claim is H2: the argument builds a cofinal countable subsystem of a presentation and the single nontrivial step -- descent of an inclusion of ideals along a faithfully flat morphism -- is displayed with its reason.
